about: Inputs for the Edge AI section of site/benchmarks.html (tools/edge_ai_section.py, called by tools/render_benchmarks.py). Timings are not here: they are rows in data/results/<board>.csv. This file holds what the store does not: each model's size, each chip's core features, the boards on order to project, and which TI AI examples ship for which board. Every block names its source.

models.source: mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/edgeai/uci-room-occupancy/<model>/layers.json (macs, scratch_ram_bytes, weight_and_param_bytes) and mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/edgeai/README.md (parameters: weights plus biases after batch norm is folded). MACs counted per layer from the shapes in layers.json: occ_cnn_500 = 8x4x5x32 + 16x8x3x16 + 16x4 = 11,328; the same sum checked for the other three.
models.kind: 1-D convolutional nets, int8 weights and integer arithmetic only, 4 sensor channels by 32 time steps in, 4 classes out (0 to 3 people in a room)

chips.source: data/boards.csv for core and clock; FPU and accelerators from each board's bench notes: cc1354p10/bench/results/ai_occ_nnc-occ_cnn_8k.txt (Cortex-M33F), c2000-launchpad/bench/fft-and-adc.md (TI FPU DSP library), c2000-launchpad/bench/control-loop.md (TMU), mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/ctrl/README.md (MATHACL), mspm0g3507/mcu-bench/README.md (no NPU on the G3507; it is on the MSPM0G5187); compilers from each board's result files (cc2340r5/bench/results/ai_occ_c-O3.txt: prebuilt model libraries from mcu-bench/edgeai, TI Arm Clang 4.0.4; cc1354p10/bench/results/ai_occ_c-O3.txt: model C compiled with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1) and c2000-launchpad/bench/ai-models.md (NNC 2.1.2, C2000 compiler 25.11.1); the C28x stores each byte in 16 bits, so its weights take about 2 bytes per parameter (65.7 kB for 33k parameters in data/results/f2800137.csv)

mspm0g3507.compiler: TI Arm Clang 4.0.4 prebuilt model library (built for the G3507), test program 5.1.1
mspm0g3507.nnc: TI NNC 2.1.2 with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1

mspm0l1306.compiler: TI Arm Clang 4.0.4 prebuilt model library (built for the G3507), test program 5.1.1

cc2340r5.compiler: TI Arm Clang 4.0.4 prebuilt model library (built for the G3507), test program 5.1.1
cc2340r5.nnc: TI NNC 2.1.2 with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1 (the G3507 prebuilt model library)

cc1354p10.compiler: TI Arm Clang 5.1.1, model compiled for this chip
cc1354p10.nnc: TI NNC 2.1.2 C output for the G3507, recompiled with TI Arm Clang 5.1.1

f2800137.nnc: TI NNC 2.1.2 with TI C2000 compiler 25.11.1

chips.fpu_source: FPU means the chip has one, not that the int8 model code uses it. TI's data sheet for the TMS320F28P65x (SPRSP69, ti.com/product/TMS320F28P650DK) lists an "IEEE 754 double-precision (64-bit) Floating-Point Unit (FPU)" and a Trigonometric Math Unit (TMU) on the C28x core.

projections.about: Boards on order are projected in the calculator from a measured board with the same core, scaled by clock. Not measured. CPU only: an NPU would change the answer. Empty now: every TI board that was on this list has measured rows.

list.text: TI NNC has already compiled all four occupancy models for this chip's NPU (for the 33k-parameter model it kept one convolution on the CPU)

Cortex-M33 at 200 MHz with an NPU and a TMU. TI's compiler built the four models for the NPU and for the CPU, both measured here; TI's own motor fault example is not run, because the SDK ships them as prebuilt libraries with no CPU twin

vendor_demos.source: docs/showcase/README.md and docs/showcase/_fragments/*.csv (which SDK ships which example for which board); timings are ai_vendor_example rows in data/results/
